summary: Establish conditional project-clone gateway with data-classification guards and Slack approval flow
description:
Issue summary: Request to build a guarded, self-service project cloning gateway that copies Jira project skeletons and associated Confluence spaces while enforcing data-classification checks and an automated Slack approval flow.

Impact: Product teams frequently request project clones for ephemeral experiments. Current manual process requires ops to verify data classification and manually create RBAC mappings, which is slow and error-prone. A guarded gateway will reduce lead time, improve compliance, and scale request volume without growing helpdesk headcount.

Request details:
- Provide an internal web/Jira UI endpoint where requesters select a project template and specify intended data classification (low/medium/high).
- Gateway must block automatic clones for high classification and route them to a manual approval queue.
- For low/medium classification, run automated policy checks: verify no PII-enabled templates, ensure linked Confluence templates have matching space-level retention labels, and create scoped service accounts for any CI/service hooks.
- Integrate a Slack approval flow: after policy checks pass, notify an approver rotation channel with a one-click approve/deny action that triggers the clone or cancels it.
- Ensure cloned Jira project has RBAC rules pre-populated according to org-role mappings and include a default audit webhook.
- Tag resulting projects/spaces with metadata for retention and exemption handling (for later archival automation).

Background/context: Teams (ML research, experimentation pods, platform) spin up experiment projects frequently. We currently process ~40 clone requests/month by hand. Recent audit flagged inconsistent retention labels and missing RBAC mappings. This gateway should enable self-serve while centralizing guardrails.

Requirements:
- Policy engine evaluating template metadata and data-classification input.
- Slack interactive messages with secure action callbacks and 2-minute timeout for approvers.
- Mapping table for org roles -> Jira groups and Confluence space permissions.
- Audit log entries stored in central Confluence evidence page and exported to S3 for 90 days.
- Concurrency limit to avoid hitting provisioning API rate limits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Developers can launch a low/medium classified project from template and have a fully provisioned Jira project + Confluence space with correct RBAC in under 10 minutes (end-to-end).
- High-classification requests create a manual ticket for Security review and do not provision automatically.
- Slack approver actions reliably trigger success/failure callbacks and update the Jira task status.
- Generated projects include proper retention/exemption tag in metadata.

Rollout plan:
1) Build feature flagged PoC integrated with one template set and the #project-onboard-ops Slack channel.
2) Pilot with ML research pod for 2 weeks and capture metrics (time-to-provision, failures).
3) Iterate RBAC mappings and extend templates.
4) Flip flag org-wide and add retention sync job.

Risks and notes:
- Permission mapping errors could provision overly permissive groups — include a safe-mode that defaults to read-only membership and requires owners to request escalations.
- Slack action token compromise risk mitigated by rotating webhook credentials and validating approver user IDs.

Requested deliverables:
- Implementation design doc (Confluence) with sequence diagram.
- Small automation service (Lambda/K8s function) and one GitHub repo with PR template.
- Confluence evidence page and a runbook for operators.

Desired timeline: Pilot ready within 4 weeks and org rollout within 10 weeks.

acceptance_criteria: End-to-end provisioning for low/medium classified templates completes within 10 minutes in pilot with <=2 retries.
